title: K=V projection sharing + Mirror role recovery
hypothesis: One MQA-shared physical projection plus small role/head Givens addresses can recover structured K/V and head asymmetry while reducing projection and KV-cache bytes, and can beat a byte-near scalar gate control.
physical_object: one projection W0 shared for K/V roles and all query heads
mirror_coordinate: one learned Givens angle per (K-or-V, query head) address
logical_multiplicity: four logical query-head key/value roles from one physical projection/cache state
teacher: The same W0 transformed by independently sampled role/head Givens angles; this is an explicitly aligned optimistic feasibility test.

development.selection_metric: mean held-out MSE across all methods

storage.serialization: torch.save state_dict plus deterministic config JSON

kv_cache.formula: number of cached logical or base projection vectors * memory_tokens * head_dim * dtype_bytes
kv_cache.cache_policy: Mirror stores one base projected vector per memory token and derives per-role/head rotations on read

success_gate: Every fresh world: Mirror MSE <=1.10x MHA, at least20% fewer projection payload bytes than MQA, at least10% lower MSE than hard MQA K=V, and within10% MSE of/better than byte-near Gate MQA.
failure_gate: Mirror misses quality gate or byte-near Gate MQA is within10% MSE at equal or lower bytes.
boundaries: teacher deliberately aligned to role/head Givens views
cache bytes describe the specified representation, not a production kernel
